clue.text: Symbolic description of what stand-up may do?

definitions.meaning: relating to an emblem such as a carved pole representing a clan, hence symbolic

definitions.text: description of what stand-up may do?
definitions.meaning: a stand-up comedian may carry a microphone about; the slang verb for carry plus the short form of microphone, run together, spells the solution

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a symbolic account of a comedian's routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word in two: TOTE (carry) and MIC (microphone), which is what a stand-up comic does on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a totem is an emblem, so anything of that nature is emblematic or symbolic.

clue.text: Web crawler brought up account of smoker's requisite

indicators.note: brought up, in a down clue, means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a bot is a program that crawls the web
O is a short form of of, as in o'clock

explanation.surface: A spider dragging up the story of a smoker's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Web crawler' suggests a spider; here it is an internet bot.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: pipe smokers need a supply of leaf to fill the bowl.

clue.text: To exit in confusion, circling round Phil Archer?

indicators.note: circling means the jumbled letters go around the other pieces
in confusion means the letters of to exit are jumbled

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Phil Archer, of the BBC radio soap The Archers, leaves in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Phil Archer is a character in the long-running British radio serial The Archers; the definition only wants an archer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a toxophilite is a lover of archery, an archer.

clue.text: Costume ball designed to incorporate square dancing

indicators.note: to incorporate means to take the other piece inside

parts.note: something designed has been made

indicators.note: dancing means the letters of square move about

explanation.surface: A costume party planned around square dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a masquerade is a masked ball where guests wear costumes.

clue.text: Weapon seen around church function

indicators.note: seen in this clue means the weapon is seen holding the other letters inside it

parts.note: a cosh is a club used as a weapon

indicators.note: around here means turned round, so the church letters are reversed

parts.note: CE is short for Church of England

explanation.surface: A weapon is spotted around a church function.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the hyperbolic cosecant is a mathematical function.

clue.text: Oxford author in vehicle meeting with sort of accident?

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a roll, as in a rollover, is a kind of road accident

explanation.surface: An Oxford writer has a car crash.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll was the pen name of Charles Dodgson, an Oxford mathematics don.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Lewis Carroll, creator of Alice, taught at Christ Church, Oxford.

clue.text: Native American Chief, possessed of firm head of hair

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: possessed of means having, so the outer pieces hold the chief letters

parts.note: a mane is a thick head of hair

explanation.surface: A Native American chief with thick hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native American Chief' reads as one phrase; Chief belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Comanche are a Native American people of the southern Plains.

clue.text: Refuse to contemplate defeat, while restraining stubborn fellow losing his head

indicators.note: restraining means holding inside, so the defeat word contains the other piece

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat

indicators.note: losing his head means the first letter goes

parts.note: a mule is a stubborn person

explanation.surface: A stubborn man refuses to consider losing.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to dismiss a possibility is to refuse even to consider it.

clue.text: See 6
Computer network, mostly imprecise, picked up inertia

parts.note: LAN is a local area network

indicators.note: picked up, in a down clue, means read upwards
mostly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: rough, as in a rough estimate, means imprecise

explanation.surface: A vague computer network ends up sluggish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like a sound signal; here it reverses ROUG to GUOR in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: languor is listlessness or lack of energy.

clue.text: Run from dogs in crates

indicators.note: taking one thing from another means removing it, so the letter for run leaves the dogs

parts.note: boxers are a breed of dog
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Dogs escaping from their crates.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: crates are wooden boxes for carrying goods.

clue.text: Fool with money invested in drink disclosed …

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so the money letter goes into the drink

parts.note: to sip is to drink
let on means revealed or disclosed

explanation.surface: A fool spends money on drink and talks too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a simpleton is a foolish, gullible person.

clue.text: … composer mostly tucked into top old drink

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the composer's name is used

parts.note: Puccini is the Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: Continues the previous clue: a composer drinking from an old top.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a cappuccino is a frothy coffee drink.

clue.text: You no longer will be found occupying number 28?

indicators.note: occupying means the word sits within the solution to clue 28, taking up its first four letters

parts.note: this points to the solution of clue 28, meaning idea

explanation.surface: An archaic pronoun asks to be found in another light.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 28 across is THOUGHT, whose first four letters give this answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic word: this was the old familiar singular form of 'you', no longer in use.

clue.text: Imagine college, University College, worried about person in office

parts.note: a hall is a college or residence at a university
UC is short for University College
someone in office, like a party in power, is said to be in
ate, as in what ate at him, means worried

explanation.surface: Imagine a college worried about its office holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' just joins worried to what it concerns.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to imagine things that are not there is to see visions.

clue.text: There's virtually nowhere else to go for online entertainment

definitions.text: There's virtually nowhere else to go for online entertainment

parts.words: There's virtually nowhere else to go for online entertainment
parts.note: virtually means in virtual reality, so the place to go online is the internet's own imagined realm

explanation.surface: A complaint that only the internet offers amusement now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' seems to mean almost; it means the virtual world.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the online world of computer networks is a virtual place.

clue.text: Rose is confused with other plants

indicators.note: confused means the letters of rose is are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A rose gets mixed up with different plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: osiers are willows used in basketwork, plants other than the rose.

clue.text: NY club hired girls to dance in local landmark

indicators.note: girls made to dance move about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A New York club hires dancers in a famous building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' refers back to NY: the skyscraper is a New York landmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Art Deco skyscraper in Manhattan is a famous New York landmark.

clue.text: Workers' supporter is following on in group

indicators.note: in means the two small words go inside the group

parts.note: a unit is a group

indicators.note: following means is comes after on

explanation.surface: A supporter of labour joins a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a trade union member supports the workforce.

clue.text: See 16
Graduate teacher following support for tester?

parts.note: a BEd is a Bachelor of Education degree, held by graduate teachers
post, Latin for after, means following

explanation.surface: A trained teacher follows a support for someone testing.
explanation.walkthrough: A tester is a canopy over a four-poster bed, not someone who tests.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the corner posts of a four-poster hold up its canopy.

clue.text: Iron, copper and no end of silica — very productive

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: no means the following letter is taken away from the word and
end of picks the final letter of silica

explanation.surface: A chemistry list of iron, copper and silica.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: fecund means fertile, richly productive.

clue.text: Ruling family? Definitely heartless and unpleasant

indicators.note: heartless means only the outside letters of definitely remain

parts.note: nasty means unpleasant

explanation.surface: A royal family that is certainly unkind.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a dynasty is a line of hereditary rulers.

clue.text: Leaving, say, pauses, taking time out

parts.note: EG, for example, means say

indicators.note: taking out means removing the time letter

parts.note: rests are pauses, as in music

explanation.surface: Leaving, for instance, after pausing for a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: egress is the act of going out, a departure.

clue.text: Went backwards to a great extent

indicators.note: backwards means the word for went is written in reverse

parts.note: went, as a euphemism for urinated, gives peed

explanation.surface: Someone went backwards a long way.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: deeply, as in deep in debt, means to a great extent.

clue.text: Gets ill, beset by head cold after cycling — showing this?

definitions.text: Gets ill, beset by head cold after cycling — showing this?

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the jumbled word goes inside
after cycling means the last letter is carried round to the front

parts.note: onion is slang for the head

indicators.note: ill means the letters of gets are in a bad state, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone catches a head cold after a bike ride, and wonders about symptoms.
explanation.walkthrough: ONION + C, cycled, makes CONION, which besets GEST (the anagram of GETS from 'ill').
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a blocked nose is the typical symptom a head cold shows.

clue.text: Number in some game finding sudden success

indicators.note: in means the number letter goes inside

parts.note: a bag is the amount of game shot

explanation.surface: A number in a game brings a breakthrough.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something that goes off with a bang is a striking success.

clue.text: Shun Socrates, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: An invitation to avoid the philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: Athens used to banish its citizens by vote, which suits the Athenian philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to ostracise is to exclude or shun someone.

clue.text: Couple's net worth? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the words net worth is taken

explanation.surface: A question about a pair's combined wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a couple is a pair.

clue.text: Hydroelectric projects led by American President

indicators.note: led by means the American letter goes in front

parts.note: dams generate hydroelectric power

explanation.surface: An American President oversees hydroelectric schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American President' reads as one phrase, but American gives A; the definition is just President.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: John Adams and John Quincy Adams were both US Presidents.

clue.text: Difficult time accepting hard idea

indicators.note: accepting means the first pieces take the hard letter inside

parts.note: tough means difficult
H is short for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A hard time accepting a difficult idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a thought is an idea or notion.

clue.text: English railway following endless trail for sightseer's target?

indicators.note: following means the English and railway letters come after the trail
endless means the final letter of the trail word is dropped

parts.note: a scent is a trail followed by hounds

explanation.surface: A tourist follows an old trail along an English railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: views of the landscape are what a sightseer goes out to see.
